title: POC Weekly Sync - Quality Eval & Regressions
summary: Weekly POC sync to review latest quality eval results, discuss regressions on recent prompt changes, and agree on tuning and next steps. Redwood SE presented scoring breakdown and suggested guardrail adjustments. Action: send updated eval spreadsheet, adjust prompt templates, run new batch of regen tests, schedule canary rollout for tuned prompts.
next_steps: Samir to share updated eval spreadsheet and changelog by 2025-07-31
Laura to prototype guardrail rule that rejects hallucinations and share PoC by 2025-08-04
Brightline to run regression tests on 500-case holdout set and share failures by 2025-08-07
Schedule follow-up sync (30m) for 2025-08-11 to review canary results
action_items: Samir: send eval CSV + short notes (due 2025-07-31)
Laura: add a thresholded QA score + implement a simple guardrail rule in sandbox (due 2025-08-04)
Jae: run 500-case regression holdout and mark false positives/negatives (due 2025-08-07)
Maya: confirm success criteria and final stake-holder list for pilot (due 2025-08-05)
transcript:
Header: 2025-07-29 15:00 PDT | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Samir/Laura (Redwood), Maya/Tom/Priya/Jae (Brightline)

[00:00] Samir Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick check in, hope the afternoon's going well. We put the latest quality evals up this morning — you all got the link?
[00:10] Maya Lopez: Yep, saw the email. skimmed it, haven't dug into failure cases yet. thanks for sending.
[00:15] Tom Rivers: same here. quick thing, Priya has to step in at 15:30 so we'll try to cover privacy items early.
[00:22] Priya Singh: yes, big thing for us is the retention and audit trail, also KMS integration.
[00:30] Laura Chen: cool. quick agenda: results summary, regression hits from prompt change last week, proposed guardrail tweaks, next steps. we'll keep it tight.
[00:40] Samir Patel: alright Laura, take it away on the scoring.
[00:45] Laura Chen: yeah so, we used your 3-tier scoring rubric — relevance, factuality, safety — each scaled 0 to 1, weighted 0.4/0.4/0.2. overall we saw a 2.8% drop in the weighted mean compared to the baseline after the last prompt template tweak. most of the delta is in factuality.
[01:05] Jae Kim: by factuality do you mean hallucinations or mismatched entity resolution?
[01:10] Laura Chen: mostly hallucinations, some entity mismatches. example - in the cardiology set a few answers asserted a drug interaction that wasn't supported. we flagged 34 cases out of 1,200.
[01:25] Maya Lopez: 34 out of 1,200 is... not tiny. what's the baseline there?
[01:30] Laura Chen: baseline had 12 flagged. so a delta of 22. again this lines up with the prompt addition we made to be more concise — it seems to have reduced verbosity but increased risky concise confident statements.
[01:45] Tom Rivers: hmm that's the classic latency/cost vs safety tradeoff, right? shorter prompt, faster tokens, but maybe more assertive completions.
[01:55] Samir Patel: exactly. also worth noting we tested both on Hosted and Redwood Dedicated profiles — Dedicated had marginally fewer regressions probably due to model version parity, but differences are small.
[02:10] Priya Singh: can you remind me which model variant we ran for the Dedicated tests? the doc has a bunch of model ids and one was mis-typed.
[02:18] Laura Chen: we used rwd-infer-v2-7b-q4 for dedicated and rwd-infer-v2-7b for hosted in the primary runs. sorry the spreadsheet has a small typo where it shows rwd-infer-v2-q47, the exported ID munged it.
[02:35] Maya Lopez: that's fine, just want clarity for the audit. Priya, does that cause a compliance concern?
[02:40] Priya Singh: KMS and audit logs are the big ones; we need to know exactly which model and whether logs are persisted across dedicated nodes.
[02:48] Samir Patel: we can confirm logs retention and KMS key separation. Laura, can we include the export of the audit log settings?
[02:55] Laura Chen: yes I'll attach the config snapshot.
[03:00] Jae Kim: on the regression set, is the scoring threshold tunable? we had a few borderline cases where the human score was 0.6 but the system cutoff was 0.7.
[03:10] Laura Chen: thresholds are tunable client-side; for the POC we used a conservative 0.7. we can lower to 0.65 for a canary to see false positive impact.
[03:20] Samir Patel: quick question for Brightline: what's your tolerance for false negatives in factuality? how many hallucinations per 1,000 answers is acceptable?
[03:30] Maya Lopez: ideally under 5 per 1,000 for customer-facing results. internal tooling could live with more, but our product goal is 2/1k.
[03:40] Tom Rivers: and SLA for latency matters — if we bump up safety checks we need to see cost impact.
[03:48] Laura Chen: agreed. to help we created a small leaderboard in the spreadsheet that shows token-level cost per call and latency percentiles tied to each prompt variant.
[03:58] Samir Patel: folks, quick note — some of the transcribed terms in the sheet got garbled, e.g. 'K V cash' instead of 'KV cache' and 'red wood dedicated' instead of 'Redwood Dedicated'. ignore those typos.
[04:10] Maya Lopez: (laughs) machine transcription problems. ok.
[04:15] Laura Chen: going into the failure typology — roughly 60% of failures are hallucination, 25% are entity mismatch, 15% are truncation/formatting. we attached representative cases.
[04:30] Jae Kim: can you read one of the hallucination examples out?
[04:35] Laura Chen: sure — example timestamp 00:12 in the exemplar file: prompt asked "List contra-indicated drugs for patient on warfarin" and model returned a statement that 'ibuprofen is strictly contraindicated and causes immediate bleeding' — inaccurate phrasing and unsourced. human label marked as hallucination.
[04:55] Maya Lopez: that's concerning. our clinical reviewers flagged it.
[05:00] Samir Patel: two paths: 1) adjust prompt to ask for citations and hedging language, 2) add guardrail that triggers a decline when confidence or fact score is low. both have cost/latency impacts.
[05:12] Tom Rivers: what do guardrails look like in the Redwood sandbox? are they inline or post-process?
[05:18] Laura Chen: currently we support post-process rules chained to the model output — simple regex/score checks or a second-pass verifier model. we can prototype a post-process that calls a smaller verifier to validate entity claims.
[05:30] Priya Singh: second pass implies data sent to another model — that's a privacy question. can we run verifier inside dedicated pool?
[05:38] Samir Patel: yes, that's supported on Dedicated; verifier can be pinned to the same VPC and use customer-managed KMS.
[05:45] Jae Kim: can we also surface the raw probability/score? the current export has a softmax-ish confidence but it's not calibrated.
[05:55] Laura Chen: we include logit-derived scores in the export but recommend calibrating with Platt scaling on your holdout. we can help with a quick script.
[06:05] Maya Lopez: ok let's talk about the prompt change — what exactly toggled last week?
[06:10] Laura Chen: we tightened the instruction to be 'be concise' and removed the conditional hedging line. quiet change but it favored brevity and convinced the model to drop cautious language.
[06:22] Tom Rivers: so revert or soft-reintroduction of hedging?
[06:25] Laura Chen: propose a middle ground: add a short citation-first constraint and lower factuality threshold from 0.7 to 0.65 for canary while adding guardrail.
[06:35] Samir Patel: sounds reasonable. we can run a canary on 5% traffic or the 500-case holdout. which do you prefer?
[06:42] Maya Lopez: for now let's do holdout batch run — Jae can run it in sandbox and we review.
[06:48] Jae Kim: yep I can run today, should finish in a few hours for the 500-case set.
[06:54] Priya Singh: about logging — will the canary run keep separate logs and not mix with production?
[06:59] Samir Patel: yes we'll create a separate route with isolated retention. Laura will attach the route config.
[07:06] Laura Chen: (typing) attaching route and audit snapshot after the call.
[07:12] Tom Rivers: on scoring, you recommended a QA composite score — can you explain how that's computed?
[07:18] Laura Chen: it's a weighted sum: 0.4 relevance + 0.4 factuality + 0.2 safety. factuality gets an internal verifier score. we also compute a diversity penalty for repeated templated replies.
[07:30] Maya Lopez: any automated alerts when regression crosses threshold?
[07:33] Laura Chen: yes Redwood Optimize can be configured to alert on regressions tied to prompt sets and dev-defined evals. we can set an email + Slack alert at delta > 1.5% drop.
[07:42] Samir Patel: that's what we had configured for the pilot actually — but we didn't tune the alerting sensitivity well, so some early noise.
[07:50] Jae Kim: curious about false positives where the QA flagged but human said okay — how many mismatches?
[07:55] Laura Chen: mismatch rate is about 8% of flagged cases. mostly edge cases with unusual phrasing.
[08:05] Maya Lopez: acceptable, but we want to reduce that.
[08:10] Samir Patel: ok let's list concrete experiments: 1) revert hedging line partially, 2) calibrate verifier with Platt scaling on holdout, 3) add post-process guardrail that rejects if verifier < 0.5 and factuality weight triggers, 4) run 500-case holdout and 5% canary after holdout.
[08:30] Tom Rivers: sounds actionable. on the security front Priya, anything else?
[08:35] Priya Singh: just KMS separation, SAML SSO for console access, and data residency. also need SOC2 artifact evidence.
[08:42] Samir Patel: we have SOC2 and ISO artifacts; I'll share the security pack. also Redwood Dedicated can be confined to a customer VPC in AWS region eu-west-1 if needed.
[08:55] Priya Singh: perfect. please note data at rest encryption key ownership needs to be customer-owned KMS.
[09:02] Laura Chen: confirmed — Dedicated supports customer-managed keys (CMK). I'll include that in the config snapshot.
[09:10] Maya Lopez: moving to timeline — we want pilot decision in mid-August, ideally go/no-go by 2025-08-18.
[09:18] Samir Patel: that's doable. final decision checklist: regression <= 2/1k, latency P95 < 320ms on dedicated, and security checks passed.
[09:28] Tom Rivers: what about cost — any ballpark delta for adding verifier step?
[09:32] Laura Chen: second-pass verifier adds ~0.12 tokens per call equivalent cost depending on verifier size; we estimated 8-12% cost increase for verifier on sensitive routes.
[09:40] Jae Kim: could we maybe run a lighter heuristic first — like metadata checks and regex-based entity spotting before calling verifier?
[09:46] Laura Chen: absolutely — layered guardrails is recommended: cheap first-pass heuristics, then heavier verifier only when needed.
[09:55] Maya Lopez: love that. ok last part — what are the deliverables we'll expect this week?
[10:00] Samir Patel: recap: Samir send updated eval CSV + changelog (by 7/31), Laura prototype guardrail and attach config (by 8/4), Jae run 500-case holdout and upload failures (by 8/7), Maya confirm final success criteria and stakeholder list (by 8/5).
[10:18] Priya Singh: good. also please send the SOC2 snapshot and KMS config.
[10:23] Samir Patel: will do.
[10:25] Laura Chen: I'll also add a short how-to on lowering thresholds for canary and sample webhook for alerting.
[10:32] Maya Lopez: thanks everyone. Tom and I need to head to another meeting — good sync.
[10:36] Samir Patel: great, appreciate the time. we'll follow up with the links and schedule the 2025-08-11 30m canary review.
[10:42] (call ends)

Notes: transcription includes occasional mislabels e.g. 'red wood' for 'Redwood', 'K V cash' for 'KV cache'. Representative failure case IDs listed in the shared spreadsheet (link in calendar invite).
